newsitem.title: FRANCE: PSA sees hurtful currency trend reversing.
newsitem.headline: PSA sees hurtful currency trend reversing.

text.p: PSA Peugeot Citroen expects damaging currency trends which have cut nearly four billion francs from its operating margin in the last four years to reverse in the second half of 1996, chief financial officer Yann Delabriere said.
Currency trends had a negative 300 million franc impact on the carmaker's first-half results, released on Monday, due partly to fluctuations in the British pound against the franc.
"This trend is reversing now and we hope for something positive for the second half," Delabriere told Reuters Financial Television.
"For the last four years, currency movements were very adverse for PSA. We lost over the last four years almost four billion French francs on the operating margin," he said.
"But this trend is reversing," he said, adding that the lira has risen around 10 percent since the end of 1995.
Productivity gains at an annual rate of around 12 percent added around 500 million francs to the operating margin in the first half and Delabriere said the trend "will continue in the second half".

He said the group's first-half 1996 results showed an improvement over second half 1995 results "and we expect that this trend will continue...We expect we won't disappoint analysts' expectations at the end of the year."
